I'm 60 this year. Been farming these same fields for 40 years — since I was 20. My father farmed them before me. It's only 10.1 mu, not a big operation. Just me and my wife now. Our son works in Shijiazhuang, sends a little money when he can, but we can't count on it. So every yuan I spend on inputs has to come back, or we feel it.

I split the land the way I have for 15 years: about 6 mu for wheat followed by maize, and the other 4.1 mu for cotton. The wheat-maize is my food security and steady income. The cotton gives me cash in the autumn, but it's labor-heavy. With only two of us, I have to be careful.

It's March now. The wheat I planted last October is greening up. I walked the fields yesterday — tillering looks decent, better than last year at this time. We had good snow over winter, so the soil moisture is okay, not great. The extension agent at the township meeting said to topdress 15–20 kg of urea per mu at green-up, but urea is 2.5 yuan per jin this year, up again. I'm putting 12 kg per mu now. I'll watch the color. If it turns yellow at jointing in April, I'll add another 8 kg. If it stays green, I save that money. I put down 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting last fall, so with the urea that should be enough. Last year I got 420 kg/mu; this year I'm hoping for 450 if May doesn't dry out.

For wheat irrigation, I'll water once in late March before topdressing, and once more at jointing. Pumping from the well isn't cheap — electricity runs about 30 yuan per mu each time. If we get spring rains I won't do a third. Two times is usually sufficient. My neighbor Lao Wang irrigates three or four times and I don't see his yields much higher.

Maize comes right after wheat harvest in early June. That window is tight — sometimes only five or six days. I'll harvest the wheat, then rotary till with my small tiller, and plant immediately. I can't afford to let the soil dry out. I buy hybrid seed from the county supply store, about 30 yuan per mu. At planting I'll put 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows, then at big flare stage I'll topdress 15 kg of urea. I know the big farms put more, but I'm not big. I have to watch my cash. Target is 480 kg/mu — last year I got 460, so about the same.

Cotton gets planted in late April. Seed is expensive: new hybrid runs about 40 yuan per mu for 2 kg. I stopped saving my own seed because the germination was poor two years ago and I had to replant. For fertilizer, 20 kg of compound per mu at planting, then if the plants look strong I'll add 12 kg of urea at flowering. Two irrigations: one at flowering, one at boll stage. The real problem with cotton is picking. Four mu by hand — me and my wife can't finish it. I'll need to hire pickers for about 8 days at 100 yuan per day. That's my biggest expense but I have no choice.

Pesticides: wheat gets one herbicide spray in spring. Maize gets herbicide right after planting. Cotton needs both herbicide and insecticide — cotton bollworm comes every year, I watch for eggs.

All in, I'm looking at about 3,960 yuan for inputs and hired labor this year. That's a lot for us. But if wheat gives me 450 kg/mu, maize 480 kg/mu, and cotton 230 kg/mu, we'll get by. You never know, though. One bad rain at harvest and the numbers don't matter. That's farming.
